title: fleeet agent check-in event
description: A single status event posted by an agent to fleeet. Four types: session_start, heartbeat, blocked, session_end.

run_id.description: Stable UUID generated at session_start, reused for every event in this run.

agent.description: Human-readable name of the agent. e.g. 'claude-sonnet-4', 'ronan-dev-agent'.

surface.description: Optional surface the agent is running in, e.g. 'claude.ai', 'Claude Code', 'Cursor'.

project.description: What the work belongs to. In a Claude or ChatGPT Project: the Project's name. In a repo-based tool (Codex, Cursor, Claude Code, …): the repo or workspace folder name. Otherwise omit it. The server trims it, collapses whitespace, reduces 'owner/repo' (or a URL or path) to the repo name, drops '.git' and caps it at 80 chars; case is kept. When omitted it falls back to source.repo, then 'general' (shown as the agent alone).

client.description: Optional. About the reporting client, not the work. fleeet stores it for support and never shows it on the board or in GET /api/events. When skill_version is older than the latest kit, the POST /api/events response (and the MCP tool result) includes update_available {latest, changelog_url}. Old versions are never rejected; an invalid value is dropped.

skill_version.description: The fleeet-reporting skill / agent kit version, from the skill's frontmatter `version:` (fleeet-emit sends its own KIT_VERSION). Semver, e.g. '1.1.0'.

summary.description: One plain sentence, no period, readable without the prompter's context. Aim for 64 characters or fewer (one line on the board at desktop width); fleeet-emit warns above that. 240 is the hard limit.

trigger.description: What initiated this work. 'user' = human prompt/task, 'routine' = cron/scheduled, 'agent' = autonomous agent decision. Default: user.

task.description: What the run is about, as a short descriptive title (like an email subject). Aim for 50 characters or fewer; fleeet-emit warns above that. Required on session_start; optional elsewhere (fleeet remembers from session_start).

source.description: Where to look for exhaust that corresponds to this run. Fleeet uses this to reconcile self-reports against reality.

question.description: The specific thing the human needs to resolve.

options.description: If the agent has plausible answers, list them. Two or three max.

usage.description: Optional token counts for the whole session, only when your tool reports them. When present, the server sizes the task from real tokens (input + output) instead of the proxy (duration, heartbeats, artefacts, files_changed).

source.description: Where the counts come from, e.g. 'reported' (from the tool or API) or 'estimated'.
